label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Kavya, I’ve been thinking about your post, and I don’t want to turn something personal between us into a public fight. I respect you a lot, and I’m grateful for the help you’ve given me.

We were both in Foundry91 Cohort 4, and I still remember you sitting with me till 1 a.m. in the Koramangala office, helping fix DabbaDost’s Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I haven’t forgotten that.

I do want to correct a couple of things, because the details are being repeated. We posted a backend developer opening on LinkedIn and Instahyre on September 14, open to anyone. One person applied on September 19; another came through a referral about two weeks later. I didn’t DM either of them. The offers were 22% above their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined us on November 3.

On the ESOP point: we do have a small pool. It’s real and has been on paper since January. I understand why you raised it, but I don’t want people to come away thinking we promised something that doesn’t exist.

That said, I got something important wrong. I knew from day one where they worked. I should have called you before making the offers, not after the second one was accepted. I WhatsApped you then, and when I didn’t hear back, I should have picked up the phone. I’m sorry I didn’t handle that better.

We’re both building in the same small hiring market around HSR and Koramangala, and in a cohort of 11 startups this is likely to come up again. Could we agree on a simple cohort norm: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer? Not to claim ownership over anyone’s choices, just to avoid surprises between people who care about each other.

Kavya, this isn’t a post against you. You’ve been a good friend, and I want to keep it that way. I’m happy to talk over coffee or on a call this week, whenever you’re comfortable.
